title: Over-allocation of Database Connections / Connection Pool Contention
pattern: Sizing database connection pools excessively high to avoid client-side contention, or failing to establish a maximum connection limit.
why_bad: It shifts the bottleneck to the database server. Most database servers spawn dedicated processes or allocate substantial memory buffers (e.g., 1-10MB) per connection. An oversized pool can exhaust database RAM, degrade query performance due to operating system thread context switching, or lead to server-side connection drops [575, 576].
detection: Pool configurations where connection count exceeds the database server's physical resource limits (RAM/CPU cores) or is disproportionately larger than the worker thread pool.
counterexample: Modest, calibrated connection pools sized to match the maximum number of concurrent request-handling threads.
fix: Size connection pools to match database hardware capabilities and use timeouts for connection acquisition.
